# Unified AWS Serverless Three-Tier Web Application Architecture

## Executive Summary

This architecture delivers a fully serverless, globally available, secure, and cost-efficient three-tier web application on AWS. It leverages managed AWS services exclusively — eliminating operational overhead while achieving enterprise-grade security, observability, and scalability. The design follows defense-in-depth principles, enforces least-privilege access at every boundary, and is fully deployable via Infrastructure-as-Code (AWS CDK recommended).

---

## 1. High-Level Architecture Summary

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          GLOBAL EDGE LAYER                                  │
│   Users ──► Route 53 ──► CloudFront (CDN) ──► WAF + Shield Standard        │
└─────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
              │                               │
              ▼                               ▼
┌─────────────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────────────┐
│   PRESENTATION TIER     │     │   PRESENTATION TIER         │
│   S3 (Static Assets)    │     │   Cognito User Pool         │
│   - React/Vue/Angular   │     │   - Authentication          │
│   - Versioned Deploys   │     │   - JWT Token Issuance      │
│   - OAC Enforced        │     │   - MFA Support             │
└─────────────────────────┘     └─────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        BUSINESS LOGIC TIER                                  │
│                                                                             │
│   API Gateway (HTTP API) ──► Cognito JWT Authorizer                        │
│          │                                                                  │
│          ▼                                                                  │
│   AWS Lambda Functions (Node.js / Python)                                  │
│   ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐                    │
│   │  Users Fn    │  │ Products Fn  │  │  Orders Fn   │  ...               │
│   └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘                    │
│          │                                                                  │
│   Lambda Execution Role (Least-Privilege IAM)                              │
│   VPC-attached (Private Subnets) + VPC Endpoints                          │
└─────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                           DATA TIER                                         │
│                                                                             │
│   Amazon DynamoDB (On-Demand / Serverless)                                 │
│   - Multi-AZ by default                                                    │
│   - Encryption at rest (AWS KMS CMK)                                       │
│   - Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) enabled                                  │
│   - DynamoDB Streams ──► Lambda (event-driven processing)                  │
│   - DAX (optional caching layer for read-heavy workloads)                  │
│                                                                             │
│   Amazon S3 (Persistent Object Storage)                                    │
│   - Application uploads / exports                                          │
│   - Server-side encryption (SSE-KMS)                                       │
│   - Versioning + Lifecycle Policies                                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     OBSERVABILITY & SECURITY PLANE                          │
│                                                                             │
│   CloudWatch Logs | CloudWatch Metrics | CloudWatch Alarms                 │
│   X-Ray Distributed Tracing | CloudWatch Dashboards                        │
│   AWS CloudTrail (API Audit) | AWS Config (Compliance)                     │
│   AWS Secrets Manager (Credentials) | AWS KMS (Encryption Keys)           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Integrated Component Design

### 2.1 Presentation Tier

#### Amazon CloudFront (CDN & Edge Security)
| Attribute | Configuration |
|-----------|--------------|
| **Distribution Type** | Web Distribution (HTTPS only) |
| **Origins** | S3 (static assets), API Gateway (dynamic API) |
| **Cache Behaviors** | `/api/*` → No cache, forward to API GW; `/*` → Cache static assets |
| **Security** | TLS 1.2+ enforced; HSTS headers; AWS WAF attached |
| **Geo-Restriction** | Configurable per compliance requirements |
| **Price Class** | PriceClass_All (global) or PriceClass_100 (cost-optimized) |
| **Access Logging** | Enabled → S3 log bucket |
| **Invalidation** | Automated via CI/CD pipeline on deploy |

#### Amazon S3 (Static Asset Hosting)
| Attribute | Configuration |
|-----------|--------------|
| **Bucket Policy** | Deny all public access; allow only CloudFront OAC |
| **Origin Access Control (OAC)** | Enforced — no direct S3 URL access |
| **Encryption** | SSE-S3 (AES-256) or SSE-KMS |
| **Versioning** | Enabled for rollback capability |
| **Lifecycle Rules** | Archive old versions to S3-IA after 30 days |
| **Replication** | Optional cross-region replication for DR |

#### Amazon Cognito (Authentication & Authorization)
| Attribute | Configuration |
|-----------|--------------|
| **User Pool** | Managed user directory with email/password + social IdP federation |
| **MFA** | TOTP or SMS MFA (recommended: TOTP) |
| **Password Policy** | Min 12 chars, complexity enforced |
| **Token Validity** | Access token: 1hr; Refresh token: 30 days |
| **Identity Pool** | Issues temporary AWS credentials for direct S3/DynamoDB access if needed |
| **Hosted UI** | CloudFront-fronted Cognito Hosted UI for login flows |
| **Advanced Security** | Cognito Advanced Security Mode (adaptive authentication) |
| **User Groups** | Admin, StandardUser — mapped to IAM roles via Identity Pool |

---

### 2.2 Business Logic Tier

#### Amazon API Gateway (HTTP API)
| Attribute | Configuration |
|-----------|--------------|
| **API Type** | HTTP API (lower cost, lower latency vs REST API) |
| **Authorizer** | JWT Authorizer → Cognito User Pool (validates Bearer tokens) |
| **CORS** | Configured for CloudFront domain only |
| **Throttling** | Default: 10,000 RPS burst; configurable per route |
| **Logging** | Access logs → CloudWatch Log Group |
| **Stage** | `prod`, `staging` with stage variables |
| **Custom Domain** | `api.yourdomain.com` via ACM certificate |
| **mTLS** | Optional for B2B integrations |

#### AWS Lambda (Serverless Compute)
| Attribute | Configuration |
|-----------|--------------|
| **Runtime** | Node.js 20.x or Python 3.12 (latest stable) |
| **Memory** | 512MB default; tune per function via profiling |
| **Timeout** | 29 seconds (API Gateway max) |
| **Concurrency** | Reserved concurrency per critical function; provisioned for latency-sensitive |
| **VPC** | Deployed in private subnets (2+ AZs) |
| **Environment Variables** | Secrets fetched from Secrets Manager at init (not env vars) |
| **Layers** | Shared dependencies (AWS SDK, utilities) in Lambda Layers |
| **Dead Letter Queue** | SQS DLQ for async invocations |
| **X-Ray Tracing** | Active tracing enabled |
| **Code Signing** | AWS Signer for production deployments |

**Function Decomposition (Domain-Driven):**
```
/users/*     → users-service Lambda
/products/*  → products-service Lambda
/orders/*    → orders-service Lambda
/admin/*     → admin-service Lambda (restricted Cognito group)
```

#### IAM Execution Roles (Least Privilege)
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "dynamodb:GetItem",
        "dynamodb:PutItem",
        "dynamodb:UpdateItem",
        "dynamodb:DeleteItem",
        "dynamodb:Query"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:REGION:ACCOUNT:table/AppTable*"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "logs:CreateLogGroup",
        "logs:CreateLogStream",
        "logs:PutLogEvents"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:logs:REGION:ACCOUNT:log-group:/aws/lambda/*"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "xray:PutTraceSegments",
        "xray:PutTelemetryRecords"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "secretsmanager:GetSecretValue"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:REGION:ACCOUNT:secret:app/*"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### 2.3 Data Tier

#### Amazon DynamoDB (Primary NoSQL Database)
| Attribute | Configuration |
|-----------|--------------|
| **Billing Mode** | On-Demand (PAY_PER_REQUEST) — scales to zero |
| **Table Design** | Single-table design with composite keys (PK/SK) |
| **Global Secondary Indexes** | Up to 5 GSIs for access pattern flexibility |
| **Encryption** | AWS KMS Customer Managed Key (CMK) |
| **PITR** | Enabled (35-day recovery window) |
| **DynamoDB Streams** | Enabled → triggers Lambda for event-driven workflows |
| **TTL** | Enabled on session/cache items |
| **Multi-AZ** | Automatic (built into DynamoDB) |
| **Global Tables** | Optional for multi-region active-active |
| **DAX** | Optional DAX cluster for microsecond read latency |

**Example Single-Table Design:**
```
PK                    SK                    Attributes
USER#user123          PROFILE               {name, email, createdAt}
USER#user123          ORDER#ord456          {status, total, items}
PRODUCT#prod789       METADATA              {name, price, category}
PRODUCT#prod789       INVENTORY             {stock, warehouse}
```

#### Amazon S3 (Object Storage — Data Tier)
| Attribute | Configuration |
|-----------|--------------|
| **Purpose** | User uploads, exports, backups, DynamoDB exports |
| **Encryption** | SSE-KMS with CMK |
| **Versioning** | Enabled |
| **Access** | Lambda role via VPC Endpoint (no internet traversal) |
| **Lifecycle** | Standard → IA (30d) → Glacier (90d) → Delete (365d) |
| **Event Notifications** | S3 → SQS/Lambda for upload processing |

---

### 2.4 Networking & Security

#### VPC Architecture
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  VPC: 10.0.0.0/16                                       │
│                                                         │
│  ┌─────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  AZ-1 (us-east-1a)  │  │  AZ-2 (us-east-1b)      │  │
│  │                     │  │                         │  │
│  │  Private Subnet     │  │  Private Subnet         │  │
│  │  10.0.1.0/24        │  │  10.0.2.0/24            │  │
│  │  [Lambda ENIs]      │  │  [Lambda ENIs]          │  │
│  │  [DAX Nodes]        │  │  [DAX Nodes]            │  │
│  └─────────────────────┘  └─────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                         │
│  VPC Endpoints (Interface):                             │
│  - com.amazonaws.*.dynamodb                             │
│  - com.amazonaws.*.s3                                   │
│  - com.amazonaws.*.secretsmanager                       │
│  - com.amazonaws.*.logs                                 │
│  - com.amazonaws.*.xray                                 │
│  - com.amazonaws.*.execute-api                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### Security Groups
| Security Group | Inbound | Outbound |
|---------------|---------|----------|
| `sg-lambda` | None (Lambda is caller) | HTTPS 443 to VPC Endpoints |
| `sg-dax` | TCP 8111 from `sg-lambda` | None |
| `sg-vpc-endpoints` | HTTPS 443 from `sg-lambda` | None |

#### AWS WAF Rules (Attached to CloudFront)
```
Rule Groups:
1. AWS Managed Rules - Common Rule Set (CRS)
2. AWS Managed Rules - Known Bad Inputs
3. AWS Managed Rules - SQL Database
4. Rate-based rule: 2000 req/5min per IP
5. Geo-blocking: configurable
6. Custom: Block requests without valid Origin header
```

---

### 2.5 Observability & Monitoring

#### Centralized Logging Architecture
```
Lambda → CloudWatch Logs (/aws/lambda/function-name)
API GW → CloudWatch Logs (/aws/apigateway/access-logs)
CloudFront → S3 (cf-access-logs/) → Athena (queryable)
CloudTrail → S3 (cloudtrail-logs/) + CloudWatch Logs
DynamoDB → CloudWatch Metrics (built-in)
WAF → CloudWatch Logs (/aws/waf/logs)
```

#### CloudWatch Dashboard — Key Metrics
| Tier | Metric | Alarm Threshold |
|------|--------|----------------|
| CloudFront | 5xxErrorRate | > 1% for 5 min |
| CloudFront | CacheHitRate | < 80% for 15 min |
| API Gateway | 4XXError | > 5% for 5 min |
| API Gateway | Latency (p99) | > 3000ms |
| Lambda | Errors | > 1% for 5 min |
| Lambda | Duration (p99) | > 25000ms |
| Lambda | Throttles | > 0 for 1 min |
| Lambda | ConcurrentExecutions | > 80% of limit |
| DynamoDB | SystemErrors | > 0 |
| DynamoDB | ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits | Trending alert |
| DynamoDB | SuccessfulRequestLatency | > 50ms p99 |

#### AWS X-Ray Tracing
```
CloudFront → API Gateway → Lambda → DynamoDB
                                 → S3
                                 → Secrets Manager

Service Map provides end-to-end latency visibility
Trace sampling: 5% default, 100% for errors
```

#### Alerting
```
CloudWatch Alarms → SNS Topic → 
  ├── Email (ops team)
  ├── PagerDuty/OpsGenie (P1 incidents)
  └── Slack (via Lambda webhook)
```

---

### 2.6 Security Controls Summary

#### Defense-in-Depth Matrix
| Layer | Control | Implementation |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| **Edge** | DDoS Protection | AWS Shield Standard (free) |
| **Edge** | Web Application Firewall | AWS WAF on CloudFront |
| **Edge** | TLS Termination | ACM Certificate, TLS 1.2+ |
| **CDN** | Origin Protection | S3 OAC, API GW private |
| **Auth** | Identity | Cognito User Pool + MFA |
| **Auth** | Authorization | JWT validation at API GW |
| **Auth** | Fine-grained | Cognito Groups → Lambda claims |
| **Compute** | Network Isolation | Lambda in private VPC subnets |
| **Compute** | IAM | Least-privilege execution roles |
| **Compute** | Secrets | Secrets Manager (no hardcoded creds) |
| **Data** | Encryption at Rest | KMS CMK on DynamoDB + S3 |
| **Data** | Encryption in Transit | TLS enforced on all endpoints |
| **Data** | Access Control | IAM resource policies |
| **Audit** | API Logging | CloudTrail (all management events) |
| **Compliance** | Config Rules | AWS Config for drift detection |

---

### 2.7 Infrastructure as Code (AWS CDK)

**Recommended Stack Structure:**
```typescript
// CDK App Structure
AppStack/
├── NetworkStack          // VPC, Subnets, VPC Endpoints, Security Groups
├── AuthStack             // Cognito User Pool, Identity Pool, App Client
├── StorageStack          // S3 Buckets (assets, uploads), KMS Keys
├── DatabaseStack         // DynamoDB Tables, DAX (optional), Streams
├── ComputeStack          // Lambda Functions, Layers, IAM Roles
├── ApiStack              // API Gateway HTTP API, Routes, Authorizer
├── CdnStack              // CloudFront Distribution, WAF, ACM Cert
└── ObservabilityStack    // CloudWatch Dashboards, Alarms, X-Ray

// Deployment Order (CDK handles dependencies):
NetworkStack → AuthStack → StorageStack → DatabaseStack 
→ ComputeStack → ApiStack → CdnStack → ObservabilityStack
```

**CDK Snippet — Lambda with Least-Privilege:**
```typescript
const usersFunction = new lambda.Function(this, 'UsersFunction', {
  runtime: lambda.Runtime.NODEJS_20_X,
  handler: 'index.handler',
  code: lambda.Code.fromAsset('src/functions/users'),
  vpc: vpc,
  vpcSubnets: { subnetType: ec2.SubnetType.PRIVATE_ISOLATED },
  securityGroups: [lambdaSG],
  environment: {
    TABLE_NAME: appTable.tableName,
    REGION: this.region,
  },
  tracing: lambda.Tracing.ACTIVE,
  logRetention: logs.RetentionDays.ONE_MONTH,
  timeout: Duration.seconds(29),
  memorySize: 512,
});

// Grant least-privilege DynamoDB access
appTable.grantReadWriteData(usersFunction);

// Grant Secrets Manager access
appSecret.grantRead(usersFunction);
```

## 3. Key Design Decisions and Tradeoffs

### Decision 1: HTTP API vs REST API (API Gateway)
| Factor | HTTP API ✅ Chosen | REST API |
|--------|-------------------|----------|
| Cost | ~70% cheaper | Higher |
| Latency | Lower | Higher |
| JWT Auth | Native support | Lambda authorizer needed |
| Features | Core features | Full feature set |
| Use Case | Standard web apps | Complex API management |

**Decision:** HTTP API chosen for cost efficiency and native Cognito JWT support. If API keys, usage plans, or request/response transformation are needed, migrate to REST API.

---

### Decision 2: DynamoDB On-Demand vs Provisioned
| Factor | On-Demand ✅ Chosen | Provisioned + Auto-Scaling |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------|
| Cost at low traffic | Pay per request (scales to $0) | Minimum provisioned cost |
| Cost at high traffic | Higher per-unit cost | Lower per-unit cost |
| Operational overhead | Zero | Low (auto-scaling config) |
| Predictability | Variable | Predictable |

**Decision:** On-Demand for startup/variable workloads. Switch to Provisioned with Auto-Scaling when traffic patterns stabilize and cost optimization is needed (typically >50% sustained utilization).

---

### Decision 3: Lambda in VPC vs Not in VPC
| Factor | VPC ✅ Chosen | No VPC |
|--------|--------------|--------|
| Security | Network isolation | Internet-routed |
| Cold start | +100-700ms (mitigated by provisioned) | Faster |
| DynamoDB access | Via VPC Endpoint (private) | Via internet |
| Secrets Manager | Via VPC Endpoint (private) | Via internet |
| Compliance | Meets network isolation requirements | May not |

**Decision:** Lambda in VPC with VPC Endpoints ensures all data-plane traffic stays within AWS network. Cold start penalty mitigated by Provisioned Concurrency for latency-sensitive functions.

---

### Decision 4: Single-Table vs Multi-Table DynamoDB Design
| Factor | Single-Table ✅ Chosen | Multi-Table |
|--------|----------------------|-------------|
| Cost | One table, fewer indexes | Multiple tables, more indexes |
| Complexity | Higher design complexity | Simpler per-table |
| Performance | Optimal (fewer round trips) | Multiple queries |
| Flexibility | Requires upfront access pattern design | Easier to evolve |

**Decision:** Single-table design for optimal performance and cost. Requires thorough access pattern analysis upfront. Document all access patterns before implementation.

---

### Decision 5: CloudFront + S3 OAC vs Amplify Hosting
| Factor | CloudFront + S3 ✅ Chosen | Amplify Hosting |
|--------|--------------------------|-----------------|
| Control | Full control | Managed |
| WAF Integration | Native | Limited |
| Cost | Pay per use | Pay per use + build minutes |
| CI/CD | Custom pipeline | Built-in |
| Customization | Unlimited | Constrained |

**Decision:** CloudFront + S3 provides maximum control, WAF integration, and flexibility for enterprise requirements.

---

### Decision 6: Cognito vs Third-Party Auth (Auth0, Okta)
| Factor | Cognito ✅ Chosen | Auth0/Okta |
|--------|-----------------|------------|
| AWS Integration | Native (API GW, IAM) | Via OIDC |
| Cost | Free up to 50K MAU | Higher cost |
| Customization | Limited UI | Highly customizable |
| Compliance | AWS-native (HIPAA, SOC2) | Separate compliance |
| Operational | Fully managed | Fully managed |

**Decision:** Cognito for native AWS integration and cost efficiency. If advanced identity features (fine-grained RBAC, enterprise SSO) are required, consider Auth0 with Cognito Identity Pool federation.

---

## 4. Cost Estimation (Pay-as-You-Go Model)

### Monthly Cost Estimate (10,000 MAU, 1M API calls/month)

| Service | Usage | Estimated Cost |
|---------|-------|---------------|
| CloudFront | 100GB transfer + 10M requests | ~$12 |
| S3 (assets) | 10GB storage + requests | ~$1 |
| API Gateway (HTTP) | 1M requests | ~$1 |
| Lambda | 1M invocations, 512MB, 500ms avg | ~$1 |
| DynamoDB (On-Demand) | 1M reads + 500K writes | ~$2 |
| Cognito | 10,000 MAU (free tier: 50K) | $0 |
| CloudWatch | Logs + Metrics + Dashboards | ~$5 |
| Secrets Manager | 5 secrets | ~$2 |
| WAF | 1M requests + rules | ~$7 |
| KMS | 2 CMKs + API calls | ~$2 |
| **Total** | | **~$33/month** |

> **Scales to zero** when no traffic. Costs grow linearly with usage, not with infrastructure provisioning.

## 5. Deployment & CI/CD Pipeline

```
Developer Push → GitHub/CodeCommit
        │
        ▼
AWS CodePipeline
        │
        ├── Source Stage: Pull code
        │
        ├── Build Stage (CodeBuild):
        │   ├── Run unit tests
        │   ├── CDK synth (generate CloudFormation)
        │   ├── Security scan (cfn-nag, Checkov)
        │   └── Build frontend assets
        │
        ├── Deploy Stage - Staging:
        │   ├── CDK deploy (staging stacks)
        │   ├── Integration tests
        │   └── Smoke tests
        │
        └── Deploy Stage - Production:
            ├── Manual approval gate
            ├── CDK deploy (prod stacks)
            ├── CloudFront invalidation
            └── Canary deployment (Lambda aliases + weighted routing)
```

---

## 6. High Availability & Disaster Recovery

| Aspect | Implementation | RTO | RPO |
|--------|---------------|-----|-----|
| **Lambda** | Multi-AZ by default | Seconds | 0 |
| **API Gateway** | Multi-AZ by default | Seconds | 0 |
| **DynamoDB** | Multi-AZ by default + PITR | Minutes | 35 days |
| **S3** | 11 nines durability, cross-region replication | Minutes | Near-zero |
| **CloudFront** | Global edge network | Seconds | 0 |
| **Cognito** | AWS-managed HA | Seconds | 0 |
| **Multi-Region** | DynamoDB Global Tables + Route 53 failover | < 1 min | Near-zero |

---

## 7. Architecture Validation Checklist

- [x] **Serverless**: All compute is Lambda + managed services (no EC2)
- [x] **Pay-as-you-go**: All services billed on consumption
- [x] **Encryption at rest**: KMS CMK on DynamoDB, S3, Secrets Manager
- [x] **Encryption in transit**: TLS 1.2+ enforced at CloudFront, API GW, VPC Endpoints
- [x] **Authentication**: Cognito User Pool with MFA
- [x] **Authorization**: JWT validation at API Gateway + Cognito Groups in Lambda
- [x] **Centralized logging**: All tiers → CloudWatch Logs
- [x] **Centralized metrics**: CloudWatch Metrics + Dashboards
- [x] **Distributed tracing**: X-Ray across API GW → Lambda → DynamoDB
- [x] **IaC**: AWS CDK with modular stacks
- [x] **Least privilege**: Per-function IAM roles with resource-level permissions
- [x] **Multi-AZ HA**: Lambda, DynamoDB, API GW all multi-AZ native
- [x] **DDoS protection**: AWS Shield Standard + WAF
- [x] **Secrets management**: AWS Secrets Manager (no hardcoded credentials)
- [x] **Audit trail**: CloudTrail enabled for all management events
- [x] **Compliance drift detection**: AWS Config rules

---

## 8. Future Evolution Path

```
Phase 1 (Current): Single-Region Serverless
    └── As described above

Phase 2: Performance Optimization
    ├── DynamoDB DAX for read-heavy workloads
    ├── Lambda Provisioned Concurrency for p99 latency SLAs
    ├── CloudFront Functions for edge-side logic
    └── Switch DynamoDB to Provisioned + Auto-Scaling

Phase 3: Multi-Region Active-Active
    ├── DynamoDB Global Tables (2+ regions)
    ├── Route 53 Latency-based routing
    ├── Lambda@Edge for auth at edge
    └── S3 Cross-Region Replication

Phase 4: Advanced Capabilities
    ├── Amazon EventBridge for event-driven microservices
    ├── AWS Step Functions for complex workflows
    ├── Amazon SQS/SNS for async decoupling
    └── Amazon OpenSearch for full-text search
```

---

*This architecture is fully aligned with the AWS Well-Architected Framework across all six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability.*
